No puedo tocar la configuración de integraciones de Linear desde acá — el MCP expone issues, proyectos y docs, no settings de workspace. Y mi token de GitHub no tiene el scope para listar instalaciones de Apps. Lo que sí pude verificar del lado de GitHub:

- `djmaam/portfolio-v3` es **privado**, y el owner es una **cuenta personal**, no una organización.
- El repo no tiene webhooks (`[]`).

La causa más probable de que no puedas conectarlo: **un GitHub App se instala una sola vez por cuenta**. Si ya instalaste el app de Linear en `djmaam` para el workspace de Kodaiverse, esa instalación está tomada, y el workspace nuevo no puede crear una segunda sobre la misma cuenta personal.

Pasos para confirmarlo y resolverlo, en orden:

1. **Andá a https://github.com/settings/installations** y buscá "Linear". Si aparece, hacé click en *Configure* y fijate en *Repository access*: si está en "Only select repositories", agregá `portfolio-v3` a la lista. Con el repo privado y fuera de la selección, Linear no lo ve aunque el app esté instalado.

2. **En el workspace nuevo**, como admin: *Settings → Features → Integrations → GitHub → Enable*. Si el flujo de OAuth te reconoce la instalación existente, listo.

3. **Si GitHub te dice que el app ya está instalado y Linear igual no engancha el workspace nuevo**, tenés tres salidas: desconectar el app del workspace viejo, mover `portfolio-v3` a una organización de GitHub (una org es una cuenta distinta, así que admite su propia instalación), o mantener los dos workspaces y aceptar que solo uno tiene la integración.

Un detalle aparte, que aplica una vez que la conexión funcione: nuestras ramas se llaman `feat/03-base-layout`, y Linear autolinkea por nombre de rama solo si seguís su formato (`marcosarrietadev/pv3-8-...`). Lo que sí va a funcionar es el **magic word**: los cuerpos de las PR que vengo escribiendo ya dicen `Closes PV3-N`, y con eso Linear linkea y mueve el issue al mergear. Si querés que además autolinkee por rama, cambio el naming de las ramas al formato de Linear en el próximo bloque — decime.

## What shipped

- `src/lib/motion/math.ts` — `docProgress`, `auroraStyle` (pure, no DOM).
- `src/lib/motion/reduced.ts` — `prefersReducedMotion()`, the JS twin of the CSS media queries.
- `src/lib/motion/scroll.ts` — `onScroll(fn) => unsubscribe`. Event raises a flag, the rAF reads `scrollY`/`innerHeight`/`scrollHeight` once and passes one shared `ScrollState` object to every subscriber. Attaches on the first subscription (scroll + resize, both `passive`), detaches and cancels the pending frame on the last. Returns a no-op under `reduce` without attaching anything. Subscribing schedules a first frame so a new subscriber starts from the real scroll position instead of bootstrapping its own measurement — that is what keeps issues 08/09 from ever needing a listener or a `getBoundingClientRect` of their own.
- `src/styles/app.css` — `@utility container-page / section-y / section-divider`, plus an `@layer components` aurora block.
- `src/layouts/Base.astro` — full head, aurora, `nav` / default / `footer` slots, one bundled script (aurora subscription + language-choice persistence).
- Both pages reduced to `lang` + the scaffold content block.

## Verifications against the real build

- **Single listener:** `grep -rhoE "addEventListener\([\"'\`][a-z]+" dist/` → ``2 click, 2 resize, 2 scroll``. Astro inlines the page bundle into each HTML file, so the site's one `scroll` call site appears once per page (1 per page, 2 pages) — there is exactly one call site in one module, `scroll.ts`. Note the minifier emits backticks, so a literal `addEventListener('scroll'` grep returns zero matches; the character-class grep above is the honest check.
- **Redirect after the move:** the inline script diffs byte-identical against `git show HEAD~4:src/pages/index.astro` (as do the font preloads). I then extracted the script *as shipped in `dist/index.html`* and executed it against stubbed `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` / `location`: no stored lang → no navigation; `lang=en` fresh session → `replace(/en)` and sets `langRedirected`; `langRedirected` already set → nothing; `lang=es` → nothing; two loads sharing one session → exactly 1 redirect. Only `location.replace` is ever called.
- **No-JS:** both `dist/*.html` carry the full content and the three aurora divs; the `.45` resting opacity is scoped to `.has-js .aurora` *inside* `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so with JS off (or with `reduce`) the aurora renders static at full strength, and there is no first-frame opacity flash when JS is on.
- **Head:** each page has canonical=1, description=1, 3 hreflang alternates, 6 `og:*`, twitter:card=1; `og:locale` is `es_AR` / `en_US`, `og:image` points at `https://marcosarrieta.dev/og.png` (file intentionally absent). The stylesheet link lands *after* the inline script in the built head, so the theme still settles before first paint.
- **Page parity:** structural diff of the two HTML files (attributes stripped) differs only in `lang`, the two `define:vars` values, and the translated copy.

## Decisions the spec did not cover

1. **The language toggle anchor stayed in the pages.** The spec's context lists it among the duplicated things that "move here", but §1 does not list it under what Base owns, the `nav` slot must stay empty, and the toggle is Nav's markup (issue 04). I moved only its *behavior* — the `localStorage.setItem('lang', …)` click handler — into Base's script, next to the redirect it pairs with, and left the throwaway anchor in the page scaffold so the redirect remains exercisable by hand until Nav exists.
2. **Third blob uses `alternate-reverse`.** The spec says "all alternate"; the mock (`handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html:39`) uses `alternate-reverse` for blob 3. I followed the mock — two blobs running `aur1` in lockstep at 16s/24s reads as correlated.
3. **Aurora alphas via `color-mix` on the tokens**, per the convention `app.css` itself declares for one-off alphas, wrapped in `light-dark()` where the mock's light and dark alphas differ (.22/.16 and .12/.08). Lightning CSS emits static hex fallbacks plus an `@supports` upgrade, so old browsers still get the blobs.
4. **`auroraStyle` string formatting:** degrees rounded (as the mock does) and `translateY` / `saturate` rounded to 2/3 decimals, to keep style strings free of float noise (`-2.4vh`, not `-2.4000000000000004vh`). Values are unchanged at every point MOTION_SPEC §4 pins down.
5. **Content sits in a `relative z-[1]` wrapper** around all three slots, so nav and footer clear the aurora too without each component minding z-index.
6. **Canonical derives from `siblingPath(pathname, lang)`** — reusing the existing normalizer instead of hardcoding the two routes, so it keeps working when more pages land.

No dependencies added.</result>

cat > docs/superpowers/specs/04-nav.md <<'EOF'
# 04 · Nav — spec

Issue: [PV3-9](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-9) · Branch: `feat/04-nav`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.1, §4 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §1 · `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-portfolio-v3-design.md` §6, §7

## Goal

The first real component. It fills the `nav` slot `Base.astro` left empty, and it brings
in the scramble effect that issue 10 reuses for company names.

## Context

`Base.astro` exposes a `nav` slot. Both pages still render a throwaway language-toggle
anchor in their content block — **it gets deleted here**; the real toggle lives in Nav.

Available: `content.ts` (`content`, `links`, `site`), `i18n.ts` (`siblingPath`),
`theme.ts` (`getTheme`, `setTheme`, `toggleTheme`), `motion/reduced.ts`,
`motion/scroll.ts`, `motion/math.ts`.

Nav copy keys in `content.json`: `navAbout`, `navWork`, `navProjects`, `navContact`.

## Scope

### 1. `src/components/Nav.astro`

Props: `lang: Lang`.

Sticky at the top, background `--color-glass`, `backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(1.4)`,
`border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-line)`. Height 64px — the same number the
anchor-scroll offset uses, so define it once as a CSS variable (`--nav-h`) and read it
from both places.

**Left**: the ✳ glyph + `site.name`.
**Right**: four anchor links, the language toggle, the theme toggle.

### 2. Anchor links

`navAbout` → `#about`, `navWork` → `#work`, `navProjects` → `#projects`,
`navContact` → `#contact`.

**None of those sections exist yet** — they arrive with issues 08 to 13. The links ship
anyway, and the smooth-scroll handler must no-op when the target is missing rather than
throw. Do not create placeholder sections to make the links resolve.

Click → `scrollTo({ behavior: 'smooth' })` at the element's offset minus `--nav-h`.
`#top` scrolls to 0 with no offset. With `reduce`, jump without smoothing.

Hidden below 720px. No mobile menu is designed: the toggles stay, the links disappear.

### 3. Language toggle

Moves here from the page scaffold, unchanged in behavior: a real `<a>` to
`siblingPath(pathname, otherLang)` that writes `localStorage.lang` on click. Label is
the language pair, active one emphasized (`ES / en`).

Base's inline script already owns the click handler that persists the choice; keep that
wiring rather than duplicating it.

### 4. Theme toggle

A `<button>` with a half-filled circle icon (CSS, not an image): a circle where half is
`currentColor` and half is transparent, rotated to read as a moon/sun hybrid.

`aria-label` from a new key — **`content.json` has no key for it and is read-only**, so
the label goes in `src/lib/ui.ts` as `{ es: {...}, en: {...} }` alongside `site`. Same
rationale as `site`: UI chrome, not translatable page copy. Ship both languages.

`aria-pressed` reflects dark mode. On click, `toggleTheme()` and update `aria-pressed`.
The button reads its initial state from `document.documentElement.dataset.theme`, which
Base's inline script has already set before first paint — never from `matchMedia`
directly, or the button and the page can disagree.

### 5. `src/lib/motion/scramble.ts` + math

The pure frame function goes in `math.ts`, the timing driver in `scramble.ts`.

```ts
// math.ts
scrambleFrame(target: string, p: number, rand?: () => number): string
```

- Glyph pool: `<>/_-=+*#%&{}[]|\01`
- Resolved prefix length: `n = Math.floor(p ** 2 * target.length)` — quadratic, so it
  resolves left to right and accelerates.
- Characters past `n` are replaced by a random glyph; **spaces are always preserved**,
  resolved or not.
- `rand` is injectable so tests are deterministic. Defaults to `Math.random`.

```ts
// scramble.ts
scramble(el: HTMLElement, duration: number): void
```

Drives `scrambleFrame` over `duration` with rAF, writing `textContent`. No-op under
`reduce` (leaves the resolved text).

Schedule on the brand: 1100ms at load after a 300ms delay, 900ms every 9s, 700ms on
`mouseenter`. The brand element carries `min-width: 9.2em` so the layout never shifts.

Issue 10 imports the same `scramble` for company names — do not write a second copy
there.

### 6. ✳ glyph

`animation: think 2.6s cubic-bezier(.6,.05,.3,1) infinite`, `text-shadow: 0 0 10px var(--color-accent)`.
The keyframe already exists in `app.css`. `aria-hidden`.

### 7. Pages

Both pages pass `<Nav slot="nav" lang={lang} />` into `Base`, and drop the throwaway
toggle anchor.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test`: `scrambleFrame(s, p, rand)` preserves length and space positions for p ∈ {0, .25, .5, .75, 1}.
- [ ] `bun test`: `scrambleFrame(s, 1, rand) === s`, and at p=0 every non-space character comes from the glyph pool.
- [ ] `bun test`: the resolved prefix grows monotonically with p, and `n = floor(p² · len)` exactly.
- [ ] `bun test`: `anchorOffset(top, navH)` — the scroll target maths — returns `top - navH`, and 0 for `#top`.
- [ ] `bun test`: with `reduce`, `scramble` leaves `textContent` untouched.
- [ ] Nav copy comes from `content.json`; the theme-toggle label from `ui.ts`. No literal strings in the component.
- [ ] The theme toggle's `aria-pressed` matches `documentElement.dataset.theme` on load, in both themes, and flips on click.
- [ ] Clicking a nav link whose section does not exist yet does not throw.
- [ ] The brand's width does not change while scrambling.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled: nav renders, the language toggle works, the anchors are plain links, the brand shows its resolved text.
- [ ] Links are hidden below 720px; both toggles remain reachable.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass.

## Out of scope

Focus rings and the full a11y audit (issue 16). The sections the anchors point at
(issues 08-13). Any mobile menu.

## Verification

```
bun run lint   → passes
bun test       → 109 pass, 0 fail (8 new)
bun run build  → 2 pages built
```

**No JS**: the nav is fully server-rendered. Brand shows resolved text, the four links are plain anchors, the language toggle is a plain `<a>`. `#top` works natively — with no element of that id, HTML makes `top` the indicated part of the document.

**Theme toggle**: the shipped bundle was run against a DOM stub that first replays exactly what Base's inline head script does. Eight checks pass, including the two that matter — stored `light` under a dark system, and stored `dark` under a light system — where button and page must agree. Both do.

**Dead links**: clicking a nav link whose section does not exist yet returns before `preventDefault()`, so the anchor stays a plain anchor and the browser no-ops. Nothing throws.

**Still one scroll listener**: `addEventListener('scroll'` appears once across the whole site, in `scroll.ts`. Nav adds none.

## Notes

- **`anchorOffset` clamps at 0.** The acceptance criterion asks a two-argument function to return both `top - navH` and 0 for `#top`, which it cannot see. `Math.max(0, top - navH)` satisfies both — `#top` reports a document top of 0 — and is right for any anchor sitting under the nav anyway. The `#top` branch stays in the DOM handler.
- **Half-filled circle via gradient, not the mock's trick.** The reference fakes the empty half with an inset shadow in the page background color; over the glass nav that reads wrong. Shipped `linear-gradient(to right, currentColor 50%, transparent 50%)` plus a 1px inset ring.
- **The language label is derived** — `${lang.toUpperCase()} / ${otherLang}` — so `ES / en` involves no hardcoded copy.
- **`--nav-h` lives in `app.css`**, not Nav's scoped style: the script reads it off `documentElement`, and Astro's scoping would not let a component `:root` rule match `<html>`.
- The `lang` attribute was dropped from the language anchor — it would have mislabeled the whole "ES / en" pair.

No dependencies added. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/04-nav.md`

cat > docs/superpowers/specs/05-hero.md <<'EOF'
# 05 · Hero — spec

Issue: [PV3-10](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-10) · Branch: `feat/05-hero`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.2 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §2 · `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-portfolio-v3-design.md` §6

## Goal

The left column of the hero and the boot sequence that reveals it. The right column —
the console — is issue 06 and stays empty here; the grid already accounts for it.

## Context

`Base.astro` renders `Nav` in its `nav` slot and a scaffold content block in the default
slot. That scaffold block is replaced by the hero.

Available: `content.ts`, `ui.ts`, `theme.ts`, `motion/{math,scroll,scramble,reduced}.ts`.

Hero copy keys: `eyebrow`, `h1a`, `h1b`, `heroSub`, `ctaWork`, `ctaContact`,
`statYears`, `statCompanies`, `statPlatforms`.

## Scope

### 0. Refactor first: shared anchor handling

Nav currently owns the smooth-scroll click handler in its own script. The hero's CTAs
need the same behavior, so **extract it before adding the hero**:

`src/lib/motion/anchors.ts` — binds one delegated `click` listener on `document` for
`[data-nav-link]`, applying the `--nav-h` offset, the `#top` special case, the
missing-target no-op, and the `reduce` guard. Called once from `Base.astro`.

Nav keeps `data-nav-link` on its links and loses its handler. The hero's CTAs get the
same attribute. One handler, one behavior, no duplication — this is why it moves rather
than getting copied.

### 1. `src/components/Hero.astro`

Props: `lang: Lang`.

Grid: `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 380px), 1fr))`. One column below that width,
console under the text.

Padding: `clamp(72px, 10vw, 140px)` top, `clamp(64px, 8vw, 110px)` bottom. This appears
once in the site, so it stays local — not a utility.

Left column, in order:

1. **Eyebrow** — mono, `--text-label`, typed character by character with a permanent
   blinking cursor (7×12px, `blink 1s steps(1) infinite`).
2. **H1** — two lines: `h1a`, then `h1b` in `--color-accent` with
   `text-shadow: 0 0 40px` accent at .3–.45 alpha. `text-wrap: balance`, `--text-h1`.
3. **Sub** — `heroSub`, `--text-hero-sub`, `--color-dim`.
4. **CTAs** — primary filled with `--color-ink` (label `ctaWork` → `#work`), secondary
   outlined (label `ctaContact` → `#contact`). Pills, `border-radius: 999px`. Both carry
   `data-nav-link`. Hover: primary `translateY(-1px)`, secondary border → accent.
5. **Stats** — three mono items, each a bold number plus its label.

### 2. Stat numbers

`8+`, `5` and `6` are hardcoded in the mock and **absent from `content.json`**, which is
read-only. They are language-independent facts, so they go in `src/lib/ui.ts` next to the
existing chrome copy:

```ts
export const stats = { years: '8+', companies: '5', platforms: '6' } as const
```

`companies` must always equal the number of entries in `jobs`. A unit test asserts
`stats.companies === String(content.es.jobs.length)`, so adding a company to
`content.json` fails the suite instead of silently making the hero lie.

`years` and `platforms` are editorial and have no derivable source — leave them literal.

### 3. Boot sequence — `src/lib/motion/boot.ts`

Elements carry `data-boot="n"`. Initial state (only under `html.has-js`):
`opacity: 0; transform: translateY(14px); filter: blur(8px)`.
Transition 900ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`.

Revealed at `bootDelay(n) = 500 + n * 170` ms:

| n | element |
|---|---|
| 0 | eyebrow |
| 1 | H1 |
| 2 | sub |
| 3 | CTAs |
| 4 | stats |

`bootDelay` goes in `math.ts` and is unit-tested, including `bootDelay(10) === 2200` —
the console's slot, which issue 06 uses.

`boot.ts` queries `[data-boot]`, sorts by `n`, and schedules each. Under `reduce` it
applies the final state immediately with no transition.

### 4. Eyebrow typing

Pure function in `math.ts`:

```ts
typedLength(elapsed: number, perChar: number, total: number): number

Returns how many characters are visible after `elapsed` ms — `clamp(floor(elapsed / perChar), 0, total)`.

## What lands

- **`src/lib/motion/anchors.ts`** (refactor, committed green first) — Nav's smooth-scroll handler becomes one delegated `click` listener on `document` for `a[data-nav-link]`, called once from `Base`. Nav loses its handler and keeps the attribute; the hero's CTAs get the same one. One handler, one behavior.
- **`src/components/Hero.astro`** — eyebrow typed with a permanent cursor, H1 in two lines with the accent glow, sub, two CTA pills, three stats.
- **`src/lib/motion/boot.ts`** + `bootDelay(n) = 500 + n·170` and `typedLength(elapsed, perChar, total)` in `math.ts`.
- **`stats`** in `ui.ts` — `8+`, `5`, `6` are hardcoded in the mock and absent from the read-only `content.json`.

## Verification

```
bun run lint   → passes
bun test       → 116 pass, 0 fail (7 new)
bun run build  → 2 pages built
```

**No JS**: `dist/index.html` carries the complete hero server-rendered — eyebrow text, both H1 lines, sub, both CTAs, all three stats. The only rule that hides anything is `.has-js [data-boot]{opacity:0;…}`, and it sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. `.has-js` is added by the inline head script, so with JS off nothing is dimmed. The typed eyebrow ships as full text; the driver empties it only when it runs.

**One anchor handler**: `data-nav-link` appears exactly once across `dist/_astro/*.js`, inside `bindAnchors`. `tests/anchors.test.ts` pins it at source level too.

**One scroll listener**: still one call site, in `scroll.ts`, with one `onScroll(` consumer (the aurora). The hero adds none.

**Runtime smoke**: the shipped `Hero*.js` run against a stub DOM schedules timers at `[500, 670, 840, 1010, 1180]` — sorted by `n` despite shuffled DOM order — and types one character per 28ms from 700ms. Under `reduce`: no timers, all five elements at `opacity: 1` immediately, eyebrow left complete.

## Notes

- **`stats.companies` is tested against `content.es.jobs.length`** (and `en`), so adding a company to `content.json` fails the suite instead of letting the hero quietly say 5. `years` and `platforms` are editorial with no derivable source, so they stay literal.
- **H1 glow and CTA outline** are per-theme literals in the mock that no token or Tailwind alpha modifier covers. Resolved locally with `color-mix()` per the rule `app.css` already states for one-offs — no new token, no literal color, `check-tokens` clean.
- **The `[data-boot]` resting state lives in `app.css`**, not Hero's scoped style: `boot.ts` is shared and issue 06's console needs the same base, overriding only its transform and duration.
- **The empty right column is a real `<div>`** so `auto-fit` creates the second track. Without it the text would stretch to the full 1200px and the layout would shift again in issue 06.
- **The typing driver is rAF-based**, with the 700ms wait as an offset on elapsed time rather than a `setTimeout`, so one loop owns the whole timeline. The mock's `setInterval` drifts out of step with the boot transitions.

No dependencies added. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/05-hero.md`

cat > docs/superpowers/specs/06-console.md <<'EOF'
# 06 · Decorative console — spec

Issue: [PV3-11](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-11) · Branch: `feat/06-console`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.2 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §2 · `handoff/content.json` → `consoleLog`

## Goal

Fill the hero's empty right column with the orchestration console, in its decorative
form. It also exposes the per-line callback that issue 07 uses to fire node-network
pulses.

The interactive console of `handoff/AGENT_CONSOLE_SPEC.md` is v1.1 and out of scope.

## Context

`Hero.astro` renders an empty `<div>` as the second grid track — the console replaces it.
`boot.ts` already handles `[data-boot]`, and the resting state in `app.css` is shared;
the console overrides only its own transform and duration.

`consoleLog` in `content.json` is 11 `[key, value]` pairs, language-independent.

## Scope

### 1. `src/components/Console.astro`

Card: `--color-console-bg`, `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)`, `border-radius: 28px`,
`box-shadow: 0 30px 80px` at .12 light / .6 dark, 1px border in `--color-line`.

Three parts:

- **Header** — three dots, the label `orchestrator — session 0x4D41`, and a LIVE
  indicator (accent dot + `LIVE`, mono, `--text-label-sm`). This is chrome, not page
  copy: it goes in `ui.ts`, same as the theme-toggle label.
- **Log** — six line slots, each `hh:mm:ss · key · value`, mono ~12.5px. `key` in
  `--color-accent`, `value` in `--color-ink`, time in `--color-dim`. Subtle scanlines
  over the log area (repeating-linear-gradient, very low alpha).
- **Footer** — three metrics: AGENTS, SPECS, SHIPPED. Mono 10px labels with `.12em`
  tracking, 20px values, SHIPPED's value in accent. Separated by 1px borders.

### 2. Timestamps must be client-side

The site is statically built. Rendering `hh:mm:ss` at build time would bake **one
timestamp into the HTML forever** — every visitor would see the moment the site was
deployed, and it would drift further from reality with every day the build is not
redeployed.

So: the server renders the six lines with their `key` and `value` and an **empty time
cell**. JavaScript fills the times as lines cycle. With no JavaScript the log reads as
six key/value lines and no clock, which is honest — better than a frozen wrong time.

### 3. Log cycling — `src/lib/motion/consoleLog.ts`

A new line every 1400ms, `rise .35s` on entry (`opacity 0 → 1`,
`translateY(6px) → 0`). At most six visible: the oldest drops as the newest enters.
The source cycles the 11 messages with `tick % 11`, so it loops forever.

The initial six lines are the first six of the cycle, so the server-rendered markup and
the first client frame agree.

### 4. Metrics — pure, in `math.ts`

Exactly the mock's formulas (`Portfolio.dc.html:696`):

```ts
metricsAt(tick: number): { agents: number; specs: number; shipped: number }
// agents  = 3 + (tick % 2)
// specs   = 12 + Math.floor(tick / 11)
// shipped = 41 + Math.floor(tick / 6)
```

Unit-tested, including that `agents` stays within 3–4 for any tick, and that `specs` and
`shipped` never decrease.

### 5. Boot and sweep

`data-boot="10"` → 2200ms, which `bootDelay` already returns. The console's own resting
state overrides the shared one: `translateY(24px) scale(.96) blur(10px)`, transition
1100ms.

A scan line crosses the card once: 2px tall, accent gradient with a glow,
`sweep 1.4s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1)` with a 1.1s delay, `animation-iteration-count: 1`.
The `sweep` keyframe already exists in `app.css`.

### 6. The callback for issue 07

```ts
export function onLogLine(fn: (line: { key: string; value: string }) => void): () => void
```

Same shape as `onScroll`: subscribe, get an unsubscribe back. Fires exactly once per new
line. Issue 07 subscribes to trigger a network pulse; nothing subscribes yet in this
block, and the API must work with zero subscribers.

### 7. Accessibility — deliberate deviation

`handoff/AGENT_CONSOLE_SPEC.md` asks for `role="log"` with `aria-live="polite"`. That is
right for the **interactive** console of v1.1, where output answers a user action.

Here the log auto-cycles forever with no user input. `aria-live="polite"` would make a
screen reader announce a new line every 1.4 seconds, indefinitely — hostile, and it would
bury the rest of the page.

So this block ships `role="log"` with **`aria-live="off"`** and a comment explaining why.
v1.1 flips it to `polite` when lines become responses to a question. The decorative log
is presentational; nothing in it is information the visitor needs.

### 8. Reduced motion

Six static lines, no cycling, no sweep, no rise. Metrics render at `tick = 0`. The
timestamps stay empty, since nothing drives them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test`: `metricsAt(tick)` matches the three formulas exactly, for tick 0, 1, 6, 11, 12, 66.
- [ ] `bun test`: `agents` ∈ {3, 4} for every tick in 0..500; `specs` and `shipped` are non-decreasing.
- [ ] `bun test`: the cycle emits the 11 messages in order and wraps, never showing more than six lines.
- [ ] `bun test`: `onLogLine` fires exactly once per line, and the cycle runs fine with zero subscribers.
- [ ] `bun test`: unsubscribing stops delivery; the last unsubscribe stops the interval.
- [ ] `bun test`: with `reduce`, no interval is started.
- [ ] `dist/*.html` contains no `hh:mm:ss` timestamp — the time cells ship empty.
- [ ] The six initial lines in the HTML are the first six of the cycle.
- [ ] `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"`; the LIVE dot and the three header dots are `aria-hidden`.
- [ ] Console chrome copy comes from `ui.ts`, log content from `content.json`. No literal strings in the component.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled: the card renders complete, six lines with key and value, metrics at their base values.
- [ ] Still exactly one scroll listener call site, and one delegated anchor handler.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass.

## Out of scope

The interactive agent (v1.1): input, streaming, expand mode, suggestion chips. The node
canvas (issue 07) — this block only exposes the callback it will consume.

content.text:
Corriendo la `06`. Dos cosas que encontré escribiendo la spec y vale que sepas, porque son decisiones y no detalles:

**Los timestamps no pueden renderizarse en el build.** El sitio es estático: un `hh:mm:ss` generado al compilar quedaría congelado en el HTML para siempre. Todo el que entre vería la hora exacta en que deployaste, y se iría alejando de la realidad con cada día sin redeploy. La consola sale con las celdas de hora vacías y JavaScript las llena al ciclar. Sin JS se leen seis líneas de `key · value` sin reloj — honesto, mejor que una hora fija y falsa. Hay un criterio que verifica que `dist/*.html` no contenga ningún timestamp.

**`aria-live="off"`, no `polite`.** El `AGENT_CONSOLE_SPEC.md` pide `polite`, y tiene razón — pero para la consola *interactiva* de v1.1, donde cada línea responde a algo que hiciste. Acá el log cicla solo, para siempre. Con `polite`, un lector de pantalla anunciaría una línea nueva cada 1,4 segundos indefinidamente y taparía el resto de la página. Queda en `off` con el comentario explicando por qué, y la v1.1 lo cambia cuando las líneas pasen a ser respuestas.

Las métricas salen con las fórmulas exactas del mock, como función pura: `agents = 3 + tick % 2`, `specs = 12 + ⌊tick/11⌋`, `shipped = 41 + ⌊tick/6⌋`.

cat > docs/superpowers/specs/07-network-canvas.md <<'EOF'
# 07 · Node network canvas — spec

Issue: [PV3-12](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-12) · Branch: `feat/07-network-canvas`
Design: `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §3, §13 · `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html`

## Goal

The hero's background: 84 nodes on a rotating 3D ellipsoid, converging into the ✳ on
load, wired to the console, reacting to the cursor, and collapsing on scroll.

This is the heaviest block in the project. It is also the one where the math/DOM split
pays off most: nearly all of it is testable without a browser.

## Context

`Hero.astro` renders inside `container-page` (max-width 1200px). The canvas is
**full-bleed** and must escape that. Restructure: the hero `<section>` becomes
`position: relative` and full-width, with an inner `container-page` wrapper holding the
two columns. The canvas is a direct child of the section, `position: absolute; inset: 0`.

Stacking: the aurora is `z-index: 0` fixed in `Base`, page content sits in a `z-[1]`
wrapper. Inside that wrapper the hero creates its own stacking context, so the canvas
takes `z-index: 0` and the columns `z-index: 1` — canvas above the aurora, below the
text, no negative z-indexes anywhere.

Already available and **to be reused, not reimplemented**: `onScroll` (`scroll.ts`),
`onLogLine` (`consoleLog.ts`), `prefersReducedMotion` (`reduced.ts`), `math.ts`.

## Scope

### 1. Pure math — `src/lib/motion/math.ts`

Everything below is a pure function with unit tests and no DOM. Anything random takes an
injectable `rand` so tests are deterministic.

```ts
ellipsoidPoint(theta, phi, r: {rx, ry, rz}): {x, y, z}
projectNode(p: {x,y,z}, cam: {f, w, h}): {x, y, sc, depth}
asteriskTarget(i: number, total: number, radius: number): {x, y}
formationPhase(t: number): {mode: 'idle'|'forming'|'holding'|'dissolving', p: number}
connectionAlpha(dist: number, minDepth: number, dark: boolean): number
collapseFactor(scrollY: number, vh: number): number
commandHopDelay(hop: number): number       // -(hop + 1) * .55
nodeCountFor(width: number): number        // 84 desktop, 48 under 720px
```

Values, straight from `MOTION_SPEC` §3:

- Ellipsoid radii: `RX = .56W`, `RY = .48H`, `RZ = .5·min(W,H)`.
- Perspective: `f = .9·max(W,H)`, `sc = f / (f + z)`, `depth ∈ [.3, 1]` drives size and alpha.
- Connections: distance `< 150px`, alpha `(1 - d/150) · .22` dark, `· .28` light, times `min(depth)`.
- ✳: 6 arms, `R = .26·min(W,H)`, centered on the console. Timeline: converge 300→1200ms
  with an ease-in-out cubic, hold to 1900, dissolve 1900→2800.
- Collapse: `clamp(scrollY / (.75·vh), 0, 1)`.

### 2. The canvas class — `src/lib/motion/network.ts`

One class, no dependencies. Owns the canvas element, the node array, and the rAF loop.
It reads `math.ts` for every formula; it must contain **no arithmetic worth testing**.

- Sizing: `devicePixelRatio` capped at 2. Resize is driven by the existing `onScroll`
  subscription's `vh`/resize tick — do **not** add a `resize` listener.
- Loop: rAF with a 24ms throttle (30–40fps target).
- `aria-hidden="true"`, `pointer-events: none`.
- `mask-image: linear-gradient(180deg, #000 55%, transparent)`.

Per-node state: `theta`, `phi`, `dTheta ∈ ±.0005`, latitude oscillation bouncing at
`±1.4 rad`, vertical `sin` of ±9px. Global rotation `.00003 rad/frame`.

### 3. Console wiring

Four anchors on the card's edges: left 25%, left 62%, bottom 50%, top 30%. Each connects
to the nearest visible node within 280px, skipping nodes occluded by the card.

The card rect is read **once per resize**, cached — never per frame.

Every log line (`onLogLine`) fires a command: a pulse from the left-62% anchor, then a
**BFS of 3 hops** through the connection graph. Hop `n` is delayed by `commandHopDelay(n)`,
travels at `.045` per frame with a `.18` tail. On arrival the node flashes: a ring growing
to 22px, decaying `×.93` per frame.

Commands stop firing once `collapse ≥ .6`.

### 4. Cursor

A violet node with a glow. Attracts nodes within 200px with force `(1 - d/200) · 1.4`,
decaying `×.9`. Violet lines to nodes within 170px. Nearby connections gain `+.35` alpha.
The pointer tilts the camera: `tilt ±.25 rad`, `rot ±.15`.

Desktop only. On touch, no cursor node and no attraction — bind on `pointermove` with
`pointerType === 'mouse'` rather than sniffing the user agent.

### 5. Scroll collapse

From the existing `onScroll` subscription: radius `×(1 - .85·collapse)`, rotation
`×(1 + 5·collapse)`, `globalAlpha = 1 - collapse`. At `collapse >= 1` the loop parks
itself — no drawing while the canvas is invisible — and resumes when it drops below 1.

### 6. Performance

Budget: ≤4ms per frame on an M1 (`MOTION_SPEC` §13). Mobile starts at 48 nodes.

Degradation: sample frame times over the first 60 frames; if the median exceeds 33ms,
drop to 40 nodes **once** and stop sampling. No adaptive loop that could oscillate.

### 7. Reduced motion

The canvas is **not created at all** — no element in the DOM, no rAF, no subscriptions.
Assert the absence of the element, not just that it is invisible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test`: `projectNode` returns known values for a node at the front, at the back, and at the edge, including that `sc` shrinks as `z` grows.
- [ ] `bun test`: `ellipsoidPoint` puts every point on the ellipsoid surface — `(x/rx)² + (y/ry)² + (z/rz)² ≈ 1` for a sweep of angles.
- [ ] `bun test`: `asteriskTarget` distributes `total` nodes across exactly 6 arms, all within `radius`, symmetric about the center.
- [ ] `bun test`: `formationPhase` returns the right mode and a 0→1 progress at t = 0, 300, 750, 1200, 1900, 2350, 2800 and beyond.
- [ ] `bun test`: `connectionAlpha` is 0 at exactly 150px, maximum at 0px, and higher in light than dark for the same distance.
- [ ] `bun test`: `collapseFactor` is 0 at 0, 1 at `.75·vh`, and clamps above.
- [ ] `bun test`: the BFS visits at most 3 hops, never repeats a node, and terminates on a disconnected graph.
- [ ] `bun test`: `commandHopDelay(n) === -(n + 1) * .55`.
- [ ] `bun test`: `nodeCountFor` gives 84 at 1440px and 48 at 600px.
- [ ] With `reduce`: no `<canvas>` element exists in the DOM.
- [ ] Still exactly one scroll listener call site and one delegated anchor handler; the canvas adds neither a `scroll` nor a `resize` listener.
- [ ] The canvas is `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none`, and sits behind the hero text.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled the hero is unaffected — the canvas simply never appears.
- [ ] Measured frame time stays within budget at 84 nodes; report the actual number.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass.

## Out of scope

Every section below the hero. The interactive console (v1.1) — this block consumes
`onLogLine` as it already exists and does not change it.

{"id":"PV3-12","uuid":"d5999eff-f924-43b8-91ee-42ddab8985e8","title":"07 · Canvas: 3D node network, ✳ formation, commands, collapse","description":"The heaviest piece of the motion work. It is where separating math from DOM matters most.

**References:** `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §3, §13 · `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html` (the math is portable; the refs/state plumbing is not) · spec §6

**Scope**

* `src/lib/motion/network.ts`: dependency-free class. Absolute canvas `100vw × 100vh`, `mask-image: linear-gradient(180deg,#000 55%,transparent)`, rAF with a 24ms throttle (30–40 fps), `dpr ≤ 2`, `z-index` below `<main>`, `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none`.
* 84 nodes on an ellipsoid (RX .56W, RY .48H, RZ .5·min(W,H)), perspective projection `f = .9·max(W,H)`, `sc = f/(f+z)`, `z ∈ [.3,1]` driving size and alpha. Global rotation `.00003 rad/frame`; per-node drift (`dθ ±.0005`, latitude oscillating and bouncing at ±1.4 rad, vertical `sin` ±9px).
* Connections between nodes closer than 150px: alpha `(1-d/150)·.22` in dark, `.28` in light, × `min(z)`.
* ✳ formation on load: 300→1200ms they converge (cubic ease-in-out) into the 6-arm asterisk (R = .26·min(W,H)) centered on the console; hold until 1900; dissolution 1900→2800.
* Console as the center: 4 anchors (left 25%, left 62%, bottom 50%, top 30%) connected to the nearest visible node under 280px, avoiding the ones covered by the card.
* Commands: each new log line (callback from issue 06) fires a pulse from the left-62% anchor + a 3-hop BFS (`t = -(hop+1)·.55`, speed `.045/frame`, tail `.18`). On arrival, `flash = 1` (ring growing to 22px, decaying ×.93/frame).
* Cursor: violet node with glow, attracts nodes under 200px (force `(1-d/200)·1.4`, decaying ×.9), violet lines under 170px, +.35 alpha on nearby connections. Tilts the camera (`tilt` ±.25 rad, `rot` ±.15).
* Collapse on scroll: `collapse = clamp(scrollY / (.75·vh))`; radius ×`(1-.85·collapse)`, rotation ×`(1+5·collapse)`, `globalAlpha = 1-collapse`; commands stopped at `collapse ≥ .6`.
* Mobile: N=48, no cursor interaction. If it drops below 30fps, N=40.
* With `reduce`: the canvas is not mounted.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `bun test`: `projectNode` returns correct x/y/sc/alpha for known cases (node in front, at the back, at the edge).
- [ ] `bun test`: `collapseFactor(scrollY, vh)` gives 0 at 0, 1 at `.75·vh` and clamps above that.
- [ ] `bun test`: the command BFS visits at most 3 hops and never repeats a node.
- [ ] `bun test`: the ✳ formation places the 84 nodes on 6 arms with the expected interpolation at t=300, 1200, 1900 and 2800.
- [ ] Profiling: ≤ 4ms per frame on desktop.
- [ ] With `reduce`, there is no `<canvas>` element in the DOM.

# 08 · About — spec

Issue: [PV3-13](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-13) · Branch: `feat/08-about`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.3 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §5, §6

## Goal

The first section below the hero, and the generic reveal observer that issues 10 to 13
all consume. That shared module is the more important half of this block.

## Context

`Base.astro` renders `Nav` and the page content. The hero is the only section so far.

`onScroll` (`scroll.ts`) already delivers `{ scrollY, vh, progress }` once per frame to
any subscriber. About's word illumination hooks onto it — **it must not add a listener**.

Content keys: `secAbout`, `aboutLead`, `aboutBody`, `principles` (3 items, each
`{ n, h, d }`).

## Scope

### 1. `src/lib/motion/reveal.ts` — shared, used by 10-13

An `IntersectionObserver` that reveals `[data-reveal]` elements once:

- Initial state (only under `html.has-js` and `no-preference`):
  `opacity: 0; transform: translateY(18px); filter: blur(6px)`.
- Transition 800ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`.
- Observer: `threshold: .15`, `rootMargin: '0px 0px -8% 0px'`, unobserve after firing.
- `data-delay` in ms staggers the transition.

```ts
export function bindReveals(root?: ParentNode): () => void
```

Called once from `Base.astro`, like `bindAnchors`. Under `reduce` it returns a no-op and
never constructs the observer.

**Rule from `MOTION_SPEC` §5, and it matters:** `data-reveal` goes on a *wrapper*, never
on the element that also has a hover `transform`. Two transforms on one element fight.
Enforce it in review, and follow it in the markup here.

The resting-state CSS lives in `app.css` next to the `[data-boot]` rule, for the same
reason: it is shared, and cascade order against a scoped style should not be
load-bearing.

### 2. `src/components/About.astro`

Props: `lang: Lang`. Section `id="about"` — the nav link finally resolves.

Layout: mono label `01 / SOBRE MÍ` on the left, content on the right at roughly 2/3.
Uses `container-page`, `section-y` and `section-divider`.

1. **Lead** — `aboutLead` at `--text-lead`, split into words:
   `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0 .26em`. Each word starts at `opacity: .16`
   with a 350ms transition.
2. **Body** — `aboutBody` at `--text-body`, `--color-dim`. Wrapped in `[data-reveal]`.
3. **Principles** — three cards from `principles`, grid
   `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 200px), 1fr))`. Each: `n` in mono accent, `h` as
   the card title, `d` as body. Staggered `data-delay` of `110 · i`.
   Hover: `translateY(-4px)`, border to accent, shadow — so the reveal wrapper is the
   `<li>` and the transform lives on the inner card.

### 3. Word illumination — pure math

```ts
aboutProgress(top: number, vh: number): number   // clamp((.8·vh - top) / (.45·vh), 0, 1)
wordOpacity(index: number, total: number, p: number): number  // clamp(p·(total+3) - index, .16, 1)
```

Both in `math.ts`, unit-tested. `MOTION_SPEC` §6 exactly.

The driver subscribes to `onScroll`, reads the lead's `top` from a rect cached per
resize, and writes `style.opacity` on each word span. Under `reduce`, every word renders
at opacity 1 and nothing subscribes.

### 4. Splitting words without breaking selection

The lead is split into `<span>` per word at build time, not at runtime — server-rendered
so it is correct with no JavaScript. Preserve the spaces as real gaps (`gap: 0 .26em`),
so copying the text still yields the sentence with spaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test`: `wordOpacity` returns .16 at p=0, reaches 1 for word 0 once p·(n+3) ≥ 1, respects the `+3` lead-in, and clamps at both ends.
- [ ] `bun test`: `aboutProgress` is 0 below the trigger, 1 past it, and clamps.
- [ ] `bun test`: `revealDelay(i) === 110 · i`.
- [ ] `bun test`: `bindReveals` returns a no-op under `reduce` and constructs no observer.
- [ ] `bun test`: reveal unobserves after the first intersection — an element never fires twice.
- [ ] The lead ships word-split in the HTML; with JavaScript disabled every word is at full opacity and the sentence copies with its spaces.
- [ ] No `[data-reveal]` element also carries a hover `transform`.
- [ ] Still exactly one scroll listener call site; About adds none.
- [ ] The `#about` nav link scrolls to the section with the nav offset applied.
- [ ] All copy from `content.json`. No literal strings.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass.

## Out of scope

Every other section. Do not touch `Base.astro` beyond the one `bindReveals()` call, and
do not touch `Footer.astro` or the nav — another block is being built in parallel.

# 14 · Footer — spec

Issue: [PV3-19](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-19) · Branch: `feat/14-footer`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.9 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §12

## Goal

Close the page. Small block, built in parallel with issue 08 — so it stays strictly
inside its own files.

## Context

`Base.astro` has an unused `footer` slot. This block fills it by rendering `<Footer>`
**directly inside `Base.astro`**, not by passing it from the pages.

Why: issue 08 is editing `src/pages/*.astro` at the same time. Base already knows `lang`,
so the footer needs nothing from the pages. `Nav` keeps its current slot wiring —
unifying the two is a cleanup for issue 16, not for this block.

Content: `footerSig` from `content.json`, `site.name` and `site.handle` from
`content.ts`.

## Scope

### 1. `src/components/Footer.astro`

Props: `lang: Lang`. Uses `container-page` and `section-divider`.

Three parts, mono, `--text-label-sm`, `--color-dim`:

- `© 2026 {site.name} · {site.handle}`
- The ✳ glyph with `animation: think 2.6s cubic-bezier(.6,.05,.3,1) infinite` and
  `text-shadow: 0 0 10px var(--color-accent)`, plus `footerSig`.
- The rotating ASCIImoji.

The year is `new Date().getFullYear()` evaluated at **build time**. That is correct here
and wrong for the console's clock: a year is stable for months and the site rebuilds on
every deploy, while `hh:mm:ss` would be visibly stale within a minute.

### 2. `src/lib/asciimoji.ts`

The 15 faces from `MOTION_SPEC` §12, in the mock's order, plus:

```ts
export function asciimojiAt(tick: number): string   // MOJI[tick % MOJI.length]
```

Its own module, not `math.ts` — issue 08 is editing `math.ts` concurrently and this has
nothing to do with motion math.

Rotation every 1000ms. `min-width: 9ch` on the element so the layout never shifts.
`aria-hidden` — it is decoration and reads as garbage to a screen reader.

Under `reduce`: one fixed face, no interval.

### 3. Do not touch

`src/pages/*.astro`, `math.ts`, `About.astro`, `Nav.astro`, `reveal.ts`. Issue 08 owns
those right now. If the footer seems to need something from them, stop and say so
instead of editing them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test`: `asciimojiAt` cycles all 15 faces in order and wraps.
- [ ] `bun test`: the list matches `MOTION_SPEC` §12 exactly, in order, 15 entries.
- [ ] `bun test`: with `reduce`, no interval is started.
- [ ] The rendered year comes from the build date, not a literal.
- [ ] The ASCIImoji element is `aria-hidden` and its width does not change as faces rotate.
- [ ] The ✳ is `aria-hidden`.
- [ ] `footerSig`, name and handle all come from `content.ts`. No literal copy.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled the footer renders complete with one face showing.
- [ ] Still exactly one scroll listener call site; the footer adds none.
- [ ] `git status` shows changes only in `Base.astro`, `Footer.astro`, `asciimoji.ts`, `app.css` and the new test file.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass.

## Out of scope

Every section above the footer. The `/world` route mentioned in `ARCHITECTURE.md` — it
does not exist and is not linked.

Los dos corriendo en paralelo, cada uno en su propio worktree aislado.

El reparto de archivos es explícito en las dos specs, no una recomendación: la `08` es dueña de `src/pages/*.astro`, `math.ts`, `About.astro` y `reveal.ts`; la `14` de `Base.astro` (zona del footer), `Footer.astro` y `asciimoji.ts`. Por eso el footer se renderiza directo dentro de `Base` en vez de pasarse desde las páginas, y por eso `asciimojiAt` vive en su módulo en lugar de `math.ts` — dos decisiones tomadas para que no colisionen, no por elegancia. A ambos les dije que si parece que necesitan un archivo del otro, paren y lo reporten en vez de editarlo.

De paso, un contraste que quedó documentado: el año del footer **sí** se evalúa en build (`new Date().getFullYear()`), al revés que el reloj de la consola. Un año es estable durante meses y el sitio se reconstruye en cada deploy; `hh:mm:ss` se pudre en un minuto.

La `08` trae `reveal.ts`, que es lo que después habilita lanzar la 10, 11, 12 y 13 juntas.

1. **The lead is inline spans, not flex items.** The spec asks for `display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:0 .26em` *and* for the sentence to copy with its spaces. Those conflict: a flex item is a block-level box, and browsers serialize block boxes to the clipboard with line breaks, not spaces. I kept the spans and put the separating space inside each word (`" interesa"`), so layout, wrapping and per-word opacity are unchanged while the clipboard gets the real sentence — verified above. Manrope's word space is ≈ the .26em the design asked the gap to be.
2. **Grid breakpoint.** `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%,300px),1fr))` plus a content column spanning 2 tracks creates an *implicit* third track at mobile widths and overflows. So the grid is a single column below 720px (the breakpoint `DESIGN_SPEC` §5 already sanctions) and the auto-fit grid above it, with `.content { grid-column: 2 / -1 }` — which never creates an implicit track.
3. **Card typography**: `n` → `text-label-sm` accent, `h` → `text-card-title`, `d` → `text-body` dim. The mock's raw 17px/14px are not tokens; `DESIGN_SPEC` §2 allows 15–18px for card body and 19–22px for card titles, so no new type token was added.
4. **Noticed, not fixed (out of scope):** the nav is `position: sticky`, so a *native* fragment jump (JS disabled) lands the section under the nav. A site-wide `scroll-margin-top: var(--nav-h)` would fix it, but that belongs to the nav/base block rather than to one section — flagging rather than adding it in About alone.

Closes PV3-13.

The first section below the hero — and the shared reveal observer that issues 10 through 13 all consume. That module is the more important half.

## What lands

- **`src/lib/motion/reveal.ts`** — `bindReveals(root = document)`. One `IntersectionObserver` (threshold .15, rootMargin `0px 0px -8% 0px`), unobserves each element as it fires, applies `data-delay` as `transitionDelay`, returns `disconnect`. Under `reduce` it returns a no-op and never constructs the observer. Bound once from `Base.astro`.
- **`src/components/About.astro`** — `id="about"`, so the nav link finally resolves. Lead split into word spans, body under `[data-reveal]`, three principle cards staggered by `110·i`.
- **`aboutProgress`, `wordOpacity`, `revealDelay`** in `math.ts`, pure.
- **`scroll-margin-top: var(--nav-h)`** — see below.

## Verification

```
bun run lint   → passes
bun test       → 186 pass, 0 fail (12 new)
bun run build  → 2 pages built
```

**No JS**: the two resting-state rules, `.has-js [data-reveal]` and `.has-js [data-word]`, both sit inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. `has-js` is only added by the inline head script, so with JS off every word and every reveal paints at full opacity.

**Copy fidelity**: stripped the tags from the built lead in both pages and compared byte-for-byte against `aboutLead` in `content.json` — identical, spaces included.

**One scroll listener**: still one call site; About subscribes through `onScroll`.

**No `[data-reveal]` with a hover transform**: the only hover rules carrying a `transform` are `.card:hover` (a child of the `<li>` that holds `data-reveal`) and the hero's primary CTA.

## Notes

- **The lead is inline spans, not flex items.** The spec asked for `display:flex; gap:0 .26em` *and* for the sentence to copy with its spaces. Those conflict: a flex item is a block-level box, and browsers serialize block boxes to the clipboard with line breaks instead of spaces. The separating space now lives inside each word, so layout, wrapping and per-word opacity are unchanged and the clipboard gets the real sentence. Manrope's word space is about the .26em the gap was asking for.
- **Grid breakpoint.** `auto-fit` plus a content column spanning two tracks creates an implicit third track at mobile widths and overflows. Single column below 720px — the breakpoint `DESIGN_SPEC` §5 already sanctions — and the auto-fit grid above it.

content.text:
Cuatro corriendo en paralelo, cada uno en su worktree: **10 Experiencia**, **11 Proyectos**, **12 Stack**, **13 Contacto**.

Los marcadores hicieron su trabajo: cada agente reemplaza dos líneas únicas de las páginas, así que git puede mergear las cuatro ramas sin conflicto.

Tres cosas que encontré escribiendo las specs y que iban a salir mal si no las anticipaba:

**`content.json` trae colores literales.** Cada job tiene `dot: "#3EE7FF"` y `glow: "rgba(62,231,255,.6)"` — el cian del tema **oscuro**. `check-tokens` no los detecta porque solo escanea código fuente, así que pasarlos del JSON al DOM habría colado un color hardcodeado que se ve mal en tema claro. La instrucción es usar `glow` solo como bandera del rol actual y estilarlo con `--color-accent`.

**`alsoWith` es solo la etiqueta**, "TAMBIÉN CON". Los nombres de empresas que debería introducir no están en `content.json`. Le dije al agente que renderice la caja con la etiqueta y la lista vacía, y lo reporte — mejor un hueco visible que nombres inventados. Va a hacer falta que los agregues vos.

**El modo de preview va indexado por host, no por posición.** Si mañana reordenás `projects` en el JSON, un índice numérico le pondría un iframe a `creativamedialab.com`, que responde `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, y el card quedaría vacío sin que nada falle. Con la clave por host, reordenar es inofensivo.

<iframe class="frame" src="https://nera-agro.com/" sandbox="" loading="lazy" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" …>

plus `agropro.ag`, `kodaiverse.com`, `masushuaia.com`. `telecentro.com.ar` and `creativamedialab.com` mount nothing — `grep -c '<img'` is 0 too, since the PNGs are absent, so both fall back to the striped placeholder. `pointer-events:none` is confirmed in the emitted CSS (`.frame[data-astro-cid-…]{…pointer-events:none;…transform:scale(.25)}`), the shimmer only inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference)`, and `data-delay` in the HTML reads `0 90 180 0 90 180` for the six cards. `grep -rl 'addEventListener(.scroll.' dist/` → one file, `_astro/scroll.*.js`; the component ships no `<script>` at all (reveals already come from `bindReveals()` in `Base.astro`).

Tres PRs abiertas: **#11 (Experiencia)**, **#12 (Proyectos)**, **#13 (Stack)**. Falta Contacto, que sigue corriendo.

Lo más valioso del round no fue el código sino dos cosas que los agentes cazaron y yo no había visto:

**El Stack encontró un bug en el mock.** Las marquesinas usan `gap` de flex entre chips. Con `gap`, el track de dos mitades mide `2 × mitad + gap`, así que el `translateX(-50%)` se queda corto por medio gap y el loop **salta visiblemente una vez por ciclo**. Está en el mock y se hubiera copiado tal cual. La solución fue mover los 8px a `margin-inline-end` del chip: ahí el track mide exactamente dos mitades y la costura es perfecta.

**El estado de `reduce` del Stack estaba mal planteado en mi spec.** Yo pedí "filas estáticas y legibles". Estático solo hubiera dejado la fila cortada por el `overflow: hidden` con unos 40 de los 52 chips inalcanzables — cumplía "estático" y fallaba "legible". El agente hizo que bajo `reduce` la fila haga `flex-wrap: wrap` con el clon oculto, así se ven todos.

Y el `check-tokens` que escribimos en la `01` mordió de una forma que no había previsto: **escanea comentarios**. El agente de Experiencia escribió un comentario explicando la trampa de `dot`/`glow` y citó los dos colores literales — el linter lo rechazó. Tuvo que describirlos en vez de citarlos.

## Decisions the spec did not cover

1. **One new token, `--color-contact-accent: light-dark(#3ee7ff, #0a8faf)`.** Not for the card/ink inversion (I used the existing pair for that) but for the accent inside the card: `#3ee7ff` on the light card is ~1.35:1 and disappears, so the label, the email and the pill hover need `--color-accent` with its branches swapped. I first scoped it as `.contact-card { --color-accent: … }` to avoid a new name — that broke `tests/tokens.test.ts`, which maps every `--name:` in `app.css` by name and would then see two declarations of `--color-accent`. Since that test isn't mine to edit, the swapped value got its own name next to the other two. The beam and halo stay on the page's own `--color-accent`/`--color-violet`, as in the mock.
2. **Icon sources.** GitHub and Telegram are Simple Icons verbatim; LinkedIn is `mdi/linkedin` (Simple Icons dropped the LinkedIn mark) — the same source the mock itself pointed at. Inlined as paths, so no dependency and no runtime request; the mock's CDN URLs would have been a third-party fetch.
3. **No brand string is copy.** `content.json` has no `GITHUB`/`LINKEDIN`/`TELEGRAM`, so the pills iterate the `links` keys and upper-case them for the label. Adding a key to `links` grows the row; only the icon has to be drawn.
4. **Borders and the grid mask use `currentColor`/`color-mix`, not tokens** (`color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 20%, transparent)` for pill borders, `currentColor` as the opaque end of the radial mask, where only alpha matters). They invert with the card for free.
5. **Two sizes stayed local instead of becoming tokens**, both used once: the email's `clamp(22px, 2.9vw, 34px)` (the mock's `cqw` converted the way the existing tokens were) and the card padding, whose floor I lowered from the mock's 36px to 28px so a 320px screen keeps some line length inside `container-page`'s own 20px.
6. **No `<script>` in the component.** `Base.astro` already calls `bindReveals()` over the whole document, so the section only ships `data-reveal`; a second call would double-observe.

8. **Worth knowing:** lightningcss emitted the icon masks unprefixed (it only prefixed the pre-existing `.hero-net` gradient mask), so the icons need Safari 15.4+ / any current browser. I left the output as the toolchain produced it rather than hand-writing `-webkit-` copies.</result>

Closes PV3-18.

The closing card: theme-inverted, with a conic gradient rotating in its border.

## Verification

```
bun run lint   → passes
bun test       → 204 pass, 0 fail (8 new)
bun run build  → 2 pages built
```

**Icons follow both the inversion and the hover.** Each pill icon is `mask-image: url("data:image/svg+xml,…")` over a shared `.icon { background: currentColor }`. Color comes only from `currentColor` — `--color-contact-ink` inherited from the card, `--color-contact-accent` on `.pill:hover`. The three data URIs were decoded out of the built CSS and each `d` diffed against a freshly fetched upstream file: paths identical, and none of the three carries a `fill`, a `color` or a `currentColor` — the SVG's default black is only ever read as mask alpha.

**Reduced motion**: every `animation:` in the bundle, `spin 7s` and `gridflow 6s` included, sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` — I traced the enclosing at-rule for both rather than taking the report's word for it.

**No JS**: `[data-reveal]` hides only under `.has-js`, so the card renders complete. All three social anchors carry `rel="noopener"`; the email is a bare `mailto:`. Still one scroll listener call site, and the component ships no `<script>` — `Base.astro` already runs `bindReveals()` over the document.

## Notes

- **A real contrast bug the spec missed.** The card inverts, so in light mode it is dark — and `--color-accent` resolves to the *light* branch, `#0a8faf`, against that dark card. The reverse in dark mode: `#3ee7ff` on a near-white card is about **1.35:1** and effectively disappears. The label, the email and the pill hover now use a new `--color-contact-accent` whose branches are swapped. The beam and halo stay on the page's own accent, as in the mock.
- Scoping it as `.contact-card { --color-accent: … }` would have avoided a new name, but `tests/tokens.test.ts` maps every `--name:` in `app.css` and would have seen two declarations of `--color-accent`. That test belonged to another branch this round, so the swapped value got its own name instead.
- **Icon sources**: GitHub and Telegram are Simple Icons verbatim; LinkedIn is `mdi/linkedin`, since Simple Icons dropped the mark — the same source the mock pointed at. Inlined as paths, so no dependency and no third-party request at runtime.
- **No brand string is copy.** `content.json` has no `GITHUB`/`LINKEDIN`/`TELEGRAM`, so the pills iterate the `links` keys and upper-case them. Adding a key to `links` grows the row; only the icon needs drawing.
- Pill borders and the grid mask use `currentColor` and `color-mix`, so they invert with the card for free.
- **No custom focus ring**, deliberately. `DESIGN_SPEC` §4 asks for one everywhere and notes it is missing from the mock; nothing in the repo implements it yet, so it belongs to the site-wide pass in issue 16 rather than to this card. The UA default is untouched meanwhile.
- Lightning CSS emitted the icon masks unprefixed, so they need Safari 15.4+. Left as the toolchain produced it rather than hand-writing `-webkit-` copies.

9	 * nothing hides behind JavaScript.

14	const markup = body.replace(/<script[\s\S]*?<\/script>/g, '')

cat > docs/superpowers/specs/09-method.md <<'EOF'
# 09 · How I work — spec

Issue: [PV3-14](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-14) · Branch: `feat/09-method`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.4 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §7 · `handoff/README.md` rule 6

## Goal

The last section, and the one with the most state logic in the site: a pinned block whose
five cards light up in sequence as the page scrolls past it.

## Context

Every other section is merged. Both pages still carry the `method` markers — the only
pair left. The section lands between About and Experience, which is where the markers
already sit.

Reuse, do not reimplement: `onScroll` (`scroll.ts`), `bindReveals` (`reveal.ts`),
`prefersReducedMotion` (`reduced.ts`).

Content: `secMethod`, `methodTitle`, `methodSub`, `cycleIdle`, `cycleDone`,
`stepVerbs` (a **pipe-separated string** of 5 verbs, not an array), `steps`
(5 × `{n, color, h, d, tool}`).

## Scope

### 1. Colors come from tokens, never from the JSON

`steps[].color` holds the five traffic-light hexes. Unlike the experience `dot`/`glow`
trap, these *are* real design colors — and they already exist as `--color-step-1`
through `--color-step-5`, added in issue 01. Map step index → token. Do not emit the
literal, and do not add new tokens.

### 2. `src/components/Method.astro`

Props: `lang: Lang`. Section `id="method"`.

Header: mono `02 / CÓMO TRABAJO` + `methodTitle` + `methodSub`, plus the status indicator
(a dot and a mono line) on the right.

Five cards in a grid `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 150px), 1fr))` — five across from
about 850px. Each card: `n`, a dot, `h`, `d`, and `tool` at the foot behind a
`border-top: 1px dashed`.

### 3. The pinned track

Desktop, **and only when both** the viewport is at least 720px wide **and** the block fits
in the viewport height: the section gets a 280vh track containing a
`position: sticky; top: 0; min-height: 100vh` block, vertically centered, 32px padding.

Progress: `p = -track.top / (track.height - vh)`.

Mobile or a block that does not fit: no sticky at all,
`p = (.85·vh - top) / (.9·height)`, same step logic.

The fit test runs on resize (through the existing `onScroll` tick — **no new listener**)
and toggles a class, so rotating a phone does not strand the section half-pinned.

### 4. Step state — pure math

```ts
methodStep(p: number): { active: number; done: boolean }
// active = p < .06 ? -1 : Math.min(4, Math.floor((p - .06) / .84 * 5))
// done   = p >= .93
methodProgress(top: number, height: number, vh: number, pinned: boolean): number
```

Both in `math.ts`, unit-tested. `MOTION_SPEC` §7 exactly.

Card states:

| state | style |
|---|---|
| upcoming | `opacity: .22; transform: translateY(10px) scale(.97)`, `--color-line` border |
| active | `translateY(-6px) scale(1.03)`, border and `0 0 0 1px` ring in its own step color, `0 20px 60px` shadow |
| completed | normal, dot lit in its step color at `scale(1.25)` with a `0 0 12px` glow |
| done (all) | accent border at .65, `--color-accent-soft` background, `0 0 44px` accent glow, accent dots |

Transitions 600ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`, and **reversible**: scrolling back up walks
the states backwards. The state is a pure function of `p`, so this falls out for free —
do not accumulate state across frames.

### 5. Status indicator

`cycleIdle` → `${verb} · ${n}/5` for each of the five verbs → `cycleDone`.

The verbs come from `stepVerbs.split('|')`, which must yield exactly 5. Assert it: a
missing pipe would silently shift every label by one.

The dot and the text take the active step's color; at `done` they take the accent.

### 6. Reduced motion and no JS

With `reduce`: no track, no sticky, no pinning. The five cards render in their normal
state, fully legible, and the indicator shows `cycleIdle`.

With JavaScript disabled: identical. The `.22` opacity of the upcoming state must live
behind `.has-js`, like every other resting state in `app.css`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test`: `methodStep(p)` gives `active === -1` below .06, walks 0→4 across the specified bands, and `done` from .93.
- [ ] `bun test`: `methodStep` is a pure function of `p` — the same `p` yields the same state regardless of call order, which is what makes it reversible.
- [ ] `bun test`: `methodProgress` matches the pinned and the fallback formulas.
- [ ] `bun test`: `stepVerbs.split('|')` has exactly 5 entries in both languages.
- [ ] `bun test`: the indicator text for each active step matches the verb at that index, in both languages.
- [ ] No hex from `steps[].color` appears in the built HTML or CSS; the five `--color-step-*` tokens are used instead.
- [ ] Below 720px there is no `position: sticky` and no 280vh track.
- [ ] With `reduce` and with JavaScript disabled, all five cards are legible at full opacity.
- [ ] Still exactly one scroll listener call site, and the section adds no `resize` listener.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass.

## Out of scope

Focus rings and the a11y pass (issue 16). The nav has no `#method` link and does not gain
one here.

Implement the "How I work" pinned section for portfolio-v3 at `/Users/djmaam/Projects/Marcos/portfolio-v3`.

Read `CLAUDE.md` first — project conventions, including that everything you write (code, comments, commit messages) is in American English.

The full spec is `docs/superpowers/specs/09-method.md`. Read it and follow it exactly. Design sources: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.4, `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §7, rule 6 of `handoff/README.md`. The reference mock is `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html` — its math is portable, its React plumbing is not.

You are already on branch `feat/09-method`. Every other section is merged into main; this is the last hole in the page, and both pages still carry the `method` markers you replace.

Work TDD: acceptance-criteria tests first, watch them fail, then implement.

Hard rules:
- Do NOT touch `handoff/` — read-only.
- Do NOT touch any other section component.
- The step state goes in `math.ts` as pure functions, unit-tested without a DOM.
- Do NOT add a scroll listener and do NOT add a resize listener. Subscribe to the existing `onScroll` from `scroll.ts` — it already delivers `vh` and refreshes on resize. Tests guard both invariants; keep them passing.
- Reuse `bindReveals` from `reveal.ts`. `Base.astro` already calls it over the whole document, so the section only needs `data-reveal` attributes and no script for it.
- No literal colors outside `src/styles/app.css`. All copy from `content.json`.
- Do not add dependencies without justifying it.

Three things that matter most here:

1. **The five step colors already exist as tokens.** `steps[].color` in `content.json` holds the same hexes, but `--color-step-1` through `--color-step-5` were added back in issue 01. Map step index to token. Emitting the JSON value would hardcode a color and defeat the token system — the same trap the Experience block hit with `dot`/`glow`.

2. **State must be a pure function of scroll progress.** The spec requires the animation be reversible when scrolling back up. If you compute state by accumulating across frames, reversal breaks in ways that are painful to debug. Three tests sample `p` across 101 steps, map the sequence, then map the reversed sequence and re-reverse it, asserting equality — for `methodStep`, for the indicator label, and for the whole five-card grid. I re-ran that check independently: forward and reverse are identical, `.05` → inactive, `.06` → step 0, `.93` → step 4 with `done`, and all six states are reachable.

**Colors** — zero step hexes in either built page. The five appear exactly once each in the CSS, as the `--color-step-N` declarations from issue 01. Cards carry `style="--step: var(--color-step-N)"`.

**Reduce / no JS** — the only rule dimming a card is `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { html.has-js .step[data-state=upcoming] { opacity: .22 } }`. The `280vh` track and the section's `position: sticky` both sit inside `no-preference and (width >= 720px)` *and* behind `html.has-js` — traced through the built CSS rather than taken on trust. With JS off or `reduce` on: no track, no pinning, no dimming, five cards at full opacity, indicator server-rendered at `cycleIdle`.

**Listeners** — `scroll` and `resize` still appear only in `scroll.ts`; the existing guards pass.

## Notes

- **Two extra pure functions.** `methodLabel` gives the indicator criterion something testable, and `methodCardState` pulls a triple-nested ternary out of the driver and makes the grid's reversibility directly assertable. The driver now holds no logic beyond measurement.
- **State as `data-state` attributes painted by CSS**, instead of the mock's inline style writes — the colors and the 600ms curve stay in the stylesheet.
- **A two-variable indirection for the step color**: the card sets inline `--step`, the CSS defines `--lit: var(--step)`, and `[data-state='done']` overrides `--lit` with the accent. A stylesheet cannot override an inline custom property, so the indirection is what lets the done state win.
- **The fit test uses `window.innerWidth`**, not the mock's element width, so JavaScript and the `@media` query agree on the same 720px boundary. It runs on the existing `onScroll` tick, so rotating a phone cannot strand the section half-pinned.
- **`data-reveal` only on the two header columns.** A reveal on the cards would fight the scroll-driven opacity — the same wrapper rule that `MOTION_SPEC` §5 states, applied to a case it does not mention.

# 16 · Accessibility pass — spec

Issue: [PV3-21](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-21) · Branch: `feat/16-a11y`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §4, §6 · `handoff/README.md` rule 5

## Goal

The first block that reads the whole site at once. Every section was built in isolation,
so this is where cross-component inconsistencies surface.

## Context

Every section is merged. The site has ten components, two routes, two themes, and a
`reduce` mode.

**The focus ring is missing.** `DESIGN_SPEC` §4 asks for a `2px accent` ring with a 2px
offset on everything interactive, and notes it is absent from the mock. Three separate
agents flagged it while building their sections and correctly left it alone as
cross-cutting work. Today `src/components/Projects.astro` has the site's only
`:focus-visible` rule.

## Scope

### 1. Global focus ring

One rule in `app.css`:

```css
:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

`:focus-visible`, not `:focus` — a mouse click on a button must not leave a ring behind.

**The inverted contact card is the exception that proves the rule.** `--color-accent`
inside it resolves against an inverted background, exactly the contrast bug issue 13
found. Inside the card the ring uses `--color-contact-accent`.

Remove the local rule from `Projects.astro` once the global one covers it — a duplicate
that drifts is worse than none.

### 2. Contrast, as a permanent test

Do not eyeball this and do not check it once by hand. `src/styles/app.css` holds every
color as a `light-dark(a, b)` pair, so the ratios can be computed:

`tests/contrast.test.ts` parses the tokens out of `app.css`, computes the WCAG 2.1
relative-luminance ratio for each pair below, and asserts the threshold **in both
themes**:

| foreground | background | minimum |
|---|---|---|
| `ink` | `bg` | 4.5 |
| `dim` | `bg` | 4.5 |
| `dim` | `surface` over `bg` | 4.5 |
| `accent` | `bg` | 3.0 (large/medium text only — see below) |
| `contact-ink` | `contact-card` | 4.5 |
| `contact-accent` | `contact-card` | 4.5 |

`DESIGN_SPEC` §6 allows accent as text only at ≥15px or weight 500, which is the
large-text threshold of 3:1. The test encodes that, and a second assertion greps the
components: any rule setting `color: var(--color-accent)` must also set a
`font-size` ≥ 15px or a `font-weight` ≥ 500 in the same block. If a component violates
it, fix the component, not the test.

This is a test rather than an audit because tokens will change again.

### 3. ARIA and semantics audit

Verify across all ten components, and fix what is wrong:

- Toggles carry `aria-label` and, where they express a binary state, `aria-pressed`.
- Decorative glyphs (✳, the ASCIImoji, the console dots, the step dots) are `aria-hidden`.
- The canvas is `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events: none`.
- Preview iframes are `aria-hidden` and `tabindex="-1"` — never a tab stop.
- The duplicated marquee halves are `aria-hidden`, so each technology is read once.
- The console log is `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` (issue 06 §7 explains why, and
  that decision stands).
- One `<h1>` per page. Section headings descend without skipping a level.
- Every `<section>` with an id has an accessible name.

### 4. Keyboard traversal

Tab through both routes and confirm: order follows the visual order, focus is always
visible, nothing traps it, and every interactive element is reachable. The nav is sticky,
so also confirm a focused element never lands underneath it — `scroll-margin-top` was
added in issue 08 for fragment jumps; focus scrolling may need `scroll-padding-top` on
the scroll container, which is a different property.

Add a skip link to `<main>` as the first focusable element. It is the one addition here
that is not in the design: with a sticky nav and eight sections, tabbing past the nav on
every page load is exactly what skip links exist for. Visible only on focus.

### 5. Reduced motion, whole-site sweep

With `reduce`: no canvas in the DOM, no marquee, no sticky pinning, no shimmer, no
scramble, no typing, no ASCIImoji rotation, no console cycling, no aurora animation, and
every `[data-reveal]` and `[data-boot]` at full opacity.

Each of those already has a test in its own block. Add one integration test that greps
the built CSS and asserts **every** `animation:` and `transition:` that moves something
sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. That is the assertion no
single block could make.

### 6. No JavaScript

Both routes fully readable and navigable. The language toggle works. This too gets an
integration test over the built HTML rather than a manual pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test`: every contrast pair in the table meets its threshold in both themes.
- [ ] `bun test`: no component sets `color: var(--color-accent)` on text below 15px and lighter than weight 500.
- [ ] `bun test`: every `animation:` in the built CSS is inside a `no-preference` block.
- [ ] `bun test`: exactly one `<h1>` per built page; no heading level is skipped.
- [ ] `bun test`: every `<iframe>` in the built HTML has `aria-hidden` and `tabindex="-1"`.
- [ ] `bun test`: the skip link is the first focusable element in both pages.
- [ ] The global focus ring covers every interactive element; `Projects.astro`'s local rule is gone.
- [ ] Inside the contact card the ring uses `--color-contact-accent`.
- [ ] A keyboard pass over both routes: order matches visual order, focus always visible, no traps, nothing hidden under the sticky nav.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass.

## Out of scope

Playwright and Lighthouse (issue 17). Company logos (issue 15). Any redesign — this block
fixes accessibility defects, it does not restyle sections.
EOF

Corriendo la `16`. La idea central del bloque es **convertir auditorías en tests permanentes** en vez de hacer una pasada manual que se pudre al primer cambio de token:

**El contraste es computable.** `app.css` guarda cada color como par `light-dark(a, b)`, así que se parsean los tokens, se calcula la luminancia relativa de WCAG 2.1 y se afirma la tabla completa en ambos temas. También agregué una cosa que no está en el diseño: un **skip link** a `<main>` como primer elemento enfocable. Con nav sticky y ocho secciones, tabular desde el principio en cada carga es exactamente el problema para el que existen. Visible solo al recibir foco.

Y le pedí que si no tiene automatización de navegador disponible, lo diga en vez de sugerir que hizo la pasada por teclado. Prefiero un hueco declarado que una verificación inventada.

`tests/contrast.test.ts` parses the `light-dark()` pairs out of `app.css`, composites the translucent ones, and computes WCAG 2.1 luminance. Final numbers:

| pair | light | dark | min |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ink` / `bg` | **17.82** | **18.24** | 4.5 |
| `dim` / `bg` | **5.30** | **6.53** | 4.5 |
| `dim` / `surface` over `bg` | **5.63** | **6.17** | 4.5 |
| `accent` / `bg` | **3.46** | **13.35** | 3.0 |
| `contact-ink` / `contact-card` | **17.81** | **17.81** | 4.5 |
