**One failure.** `--color-contact-accent` was documented as "`--color-accent` with its branches swapped", but the swap only fixed one direction: `#3ee7ff` on the dark card is 13.03, while `#0a8faf` on the *light* card is 3.46 — large-text only, and the card carries the accent at 12px in `06 / CONTACTO` and in the pills on hover. Darkened that branch to `#087a95` → 4.55. The page accent is untouched (it only owes 3.0).

## What the reduced-motion sweep found

All **11** `animation:` declarations in the built CSS were already inside a `no-preference` block — that half was clean. The finding was the other half: **5 hover states that still move with `reduce`**, because each section wrote its transform outside its own guard.

- `Hero.astro` — CTA `translateY(-1px)`
- `About.astro`, `Experience.astro`, `Projects.astro` — card `translateY(-4px)`
- `Contact.astro` — email `gap: 10px → 16px`
- plus `Method.astro`'s active-step lift and dot scale (unreachable with `reduce` because `onScroll` never subscribes — but only by accident)

Each transform and its transition moved into the section's existing `no-preference` block. With `reduce` the element still takes its hover border, shadow and color; it just stays put.

## Fixed, by component

| where | fix |
|---|---|
| `app.css` | global `:focus-visible` ring; `scroll-padding-top: var(--nav-h)`; `.skip-link` styles; `--color-contact-accent` darkened |
| `Base.astro` | skip link as first body child; `<main id="main" tabindex="-1">` |
| `ui.ts` | `skipToContent` in es/en |
| `Contact.astro` | ring override to `--color-contact-accent`; `aria-labelledby`; email gap guarded |
| `Projects.astro` | local `:focus-visible` removed; `.kind`/`.arrow` weight 500; `aria-labelledby`; card lift guarded |
| `About.astro` | lead `<p>` → `<h2>` (fixes h1→h3 skip); `.accent` weight 500; `aria-labelledby`; card lift guarded |
| `Method.astro` | `.status` weight 500; `aria-labelledby`; step + dot transforms guarded |
| `Console.astro` | `.key`, `.live` weight 500 |
| `Stack.astro` | `.chip.core` weight 500; `aria-labelledby` |
| `Experience.astro` | `aria-labelledby`; card lift guarded |
| `Footer.astro` | `.handle`, `.glyph` weight 500 |
| `Hero.astro` | `.accent` weight restated; CTA lift guarded |

The ARIA audit found the rest already correct: iframes `aria-hidden`+`tabindex="-1"`, canvas `aria-hidden`+`pointer-events:none`, marquee clones hidden, `role="log"`/`aria-live="off"`, every decorative glyph hidden, theme toggle with `aria-label`+`aria-pressed`.

## Keyboard pass

**No browser automation is reachable in this environment** — no `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools, no Playwright (out of scope per the spec anyway). I did not drive a real browser. What I did instead was dump the focusable sequence from both built routes and encode it as a test:

```
 1 skip-link #main   2 brand #top   3-6 nav links   7 lang toggle   8 theme button
 9-10 hero CTAs     11-16 project cards            17 email        18-20 social pills
21 footer handle
```

Identical on `/` and `/en`, matches visual order, no positive `tabindex` anywhere (the only 5 are `-1`, all on preview iframes), so nothing overrides or traps the order. The nav-overlap risk is handled by `scroll-padding-top`. What I cannot certify without a browser: that the ring is *visually* unclipped everywhere (`overflow: hidden` on `.row`, `.preview`, `.edge` could crop a 2px offset ring on an element that sits flush against those edges). Worth one manual pass, or issue 17's Playwright run.

## Decisions the spec did not cover

1. **Weight 500, not larger type.** Eight rules painted small mono labels with the accent at weight 400. `DESIGN_SPEC` §6 offers "≥15px **or** weight 500" — I took the weight, since bumping sizes would be a restyle. 500 is inside the design's own 400–500 range for small mono labels. Note the design's rule is looser than WCAG, which puts large text at ≥18.66px bold / ≥24px; at 3.46:1 in light, these labels satisfy the design spec but not WCAG AA on their own. Raising the light accent would change the whole site's cyan, so I left it and flagged it here.
2. **`.handle` and `.status` take the weight at rest**, not in the hover/done state — changing weight on hover reflows the line. The test resolves the size/weight from the rule *or* from the rule for that element's own class, which is why this works.
3. **`Hero.astro`'s `.accent` restates `font-weight: 600`** (the h1's own). Redundant to the browser, but it is what makes the rule auditable without the markup beside it.
4. **About's lead became the `<h2>`.** It is what the other sections render as `<h2 class="text-h2">`, and Tailwind's preflight resets heading size/weight to `inherit`, so nothing renders differently. The alternative — promoting the principle cards to `<h2>` — would have been semantically wrong.
5. **`aria-labelledby` over `aria-label`** for the six named sections: no copy duplicated, `content.json` stays the only source, and it avoids screen readers spelling out the all-caps `secAbout` values.
6. **`<main>` got `tabindex="-1"`** so the skip link moves focus and not just the viewport (Safari otherwise only scrolls).
7. **The skip link hides with `top: -100px`, not a transform** — nothing to animate for a `reduce` visitor, and it keeps the hover/transform sweep honest.
8. **No dependencies added.** Considered axe: it needs a DOM (jsdom + axe-core, two deps) and would *not* catch the two findings that mattered here — the token pair failure, because it never sees the dark theme's inverted card without rendering both themes, and the reduced-motion sweep, which it does not check at all. The CSS-parsing tests cover both and run in 0.9s with the build included.</result>

At 3.46:1 in light mode these small labels satisfy the design and not WCAG AA on their own. Raising the light accent would change the site's cyan everywhere, so it stays — flagged rather than silently accepted.

content.text:
`16` lista. PR: **https://github.com/djmaam/portfolio-v3/pull/16** — CI corriendo. **304 tests**, +43.

El bloque encontró exactamente lo que un bloque transversal tiene que encontrar: dos defectos que **ninguna PR individual podía ver**.

**Un fallo de contraste real.** `--color-contact-accent` lo agregó la `13` documentándolo como "el acento con las ramas intercambiadas". Pero intercambiar arreglaba una sola dirección: `#0a8faf` sobre la tarjeta clara daba **3.46**, y la tarjeta usa el acento a 12px en `06 / CONTACTO` y en el hover de los pills. Ahora esa rama es `#087a95` → **4.55**. Recalculé todos los ratios por mi cuenta y coinciden con los suyos.

**Cinco hovers que seguían moviéndose con `reduce`.** Las 11 animaciones ya estaban bien encerradas — cada sección testeó la suya. Lo que se escapó fueron los `transform` de hover: el lift del CTA del hero, el de las tarjetas de About, Experiencia y Proyectos, y el gap del email en Contacto. Cada sección escribió su transform fuera de su propio guard. Ninguna podía detectarlo sola porque cada una veía solo su archivo. Verifiqué el CSS construido: ahora hay **cero** `:hover` con `transform` y **cero** `animation:` fuera de un bloque `no-preference`.

Dos cosas que quedan declaradas, no resueltas:

- **No hubo pasada real por teclado** — no había automatización de navegador disponible. En su lugar volcó la secuencia de foco de ambas rutas y la fijó como test. Lo que no puede certificar sin navegador es que el anillo no quede **recortado** por los `overflow: hidden` de `.row`, `.preview` y `.edge`. Eso lo agarra Playwright en la `17`.
- **La regla de acento del diseño es más laxa que WCAG.** `DESIGN_SPEC` §6 permite acento a ≥15px *o* peso 500; WCAG pide ≥18.66px en negrita. A 3.46:1 en claro, esas etiquetas mono chicas cumplen el diseño y no WCAG AA por sí solas. Subir el cian claro cambiaría el color de todo el sitio, así que queda flaggeado y no silenciado.
